question: Does router.java_quirks.shove_via_into_pending_piece=false (before a shove substitute piece goes on the board, its shapes are queried again and the shove fails at a via of another net that a deeper level of TraceShover.insert's recursion moved onto it, where Java inserts the piece over the via, a short) keep every registered board's routing within N02's totals rule (accept no-regress: a correctness fix) of Java's behaviour, under profile legacy and under profile enhanced, with no new router clearance violation and no new KiCad shorting_items or clearance error; and how often does the branch decide a result?
engine: freerouting-rs at the implementing commit (main dcf0641 plus N06.15's diff at registration), one Linux release build for every arm; P04's bounds (3 passes, optimizer off), the bounds N03.2 measured GP8B with; each arm gives the switch explicitly

legacy_baseline.engine: freerouting-rs at the implementing commit (main dcf0641 plus N06.15's diff at registration), one Linux release build for every arm
legacy_baseline.what: baseline: profile legacy, the switch true (Java's shove)

legacy_fix.engine: freerouting-rs at the implementing commit (main dcf0641 plus N06.15's diff at registration), one Linux release build for every arm
legacy_fix.what: candidate under legacy: the shove fails at a via of another net on a pending piece

enhanced_baseline.engine: freerouting-rs at the implementing commit (main dcf0641 plus N06.15's diff at registration), one Linux release build for every arm
enhanced_baseline.what: baseline under enhanced (the default profile, which the fix would join): the switch true

enhanced_fix.engine: freerouting-rs at the implementing commit (main dcf0641 plus N06.15's diff at registration), one Linux release build for every arm
enhanced_fix.what: candidate under enhanced: the answer N03.3 needs

boards.eligibility: every row; no row is dropped after a number
boards.bands: each DSN row's band is N02's default, max(2, ceil(5 % of the row's connections)), connections = the legacy_baseline arm's board_statistics.connections.maximum_count (n06_run.py copies it into summary.json's statistics.connections); the plugin row's band is 10
boards.plugin_row: canary-pwr-plugin: canary-pwr through the KiCad plugin path (plugin_canary below), outside n06_run.py
boards.seen_before_registration: N03.2's GP8B legacy runs with the env-gated prototype of this fix (bbd1336): canonical room order 51 -> 64 unrouted, tree order 61 -> 59, 2 -> 0 and 0 -> 0 router violations; the implementer's light runs while choosing rows: the reach counter shove_via_into_pending_pieces read 0 on Issue508-DAC2020_bm01 and Issue593-BBD_Mars-64 (legacy, these bounds; no routing number was read), and one GP8B route per arm (legacy and enhanced, these bounds) to confirm that the switch reproduces the prototype, whose numbers are in N06.15's note

metric_definitions.unrouted, clearance_violations, vias: the result manifest's board_statistics (connections.incomplete_count, clearance_violations.total_count, vias.total_count): Freerouting's board model on the routed board; n06_run.py copies them into summary.json as `statistics`
metric_definitions.session_differences: 1 if the arm's SES differs byte for byte from its own baseline arm's (the arm's `baseline` key: legacy_baseline for the legacy arms, enhanced_baseline for the enhanced arms) on that board
metric_definitions.shove_via_into_pending_pieces: run_stats counter (--stats json, total.counts), in either arm: shove substitute pieces about to be inserted whose shapes overlap, with the piece's clearance, a via of another net (Java inserts the piece; the fix fails the shove at the first)
metric_definitions.shove_pending_piece_foreign_traces: run_stats counter, in either arm: such pieces whose shapes overlap the copper of a trace of another net, which neither arm acts on (the case the switch leaves open)
metric_definitions.kicad_unconnected, kicad_shorting_items,: the canary-pwr plugin row's grade (canary hardware/tools/grade.sh): KiCad DRC unconnected items, shorting_items and clearance violations, the real DRC errors, via_in_pad.py and the minimum checks

accept: Reachability first: if shove_via_into_pending_pieces is 0 in every run and every session equals its own baseline's, no registered board reaches the branch, and the fix is accepted on its tests (both behaviours pinned).
Sessions identical but the counter above 0: the branch runs but decides nothing that reaches the output; the fix is neutral and accepted.

Otherwise the totals rule for each verdict pair, (legacy_baseline, legacy_fix) and (enhanced_baseline, enhanced_fix), judged alone. Hard guards, any worsening rejects: no DSN row's router clearance_violations above its baseline's; on the plugin row via_in_pad and below_minimum 0 and kicad_shorting_items, kicad_clearance and drc_real not above the baseline's. Then the candidate's unrouted summed over the DSN rows plus the plugin row's kicad_unconnected at most the baseline's plus the set's noise, sqrt of the sum of the bands squared; no row worse by more than twice its band.
The enhanced pair decides whether N06.13 turns the switch off in enhanced (N05) and is the answer N03.3 reads; the legacy pair is recorded with it (legacy keeps the switch true either way).
stop_rule: One run per arm per row. No heavy run by the implementer beyond one GP8B route per arm.
orchestrator_command: CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/thebo/code/freerouting-rs/target/orchestrator/n06-target cargo build --release -p freerouting-cli && python3 tools/bench/n06_run.py docs/roadmap/prereg/N06.15.json --out /home/thebo/code/freerouting-rs/target/orchestrator/n06-v
orchestrator: Run orchestrator_command from the worktree root: it runs each arms.command on each boards.files row (7 rows x 4 arms = 28 runs), checks the input hashes, compares each SES with its own baseline arm's and writes summary.json (session_differences, counts, statistics). It exits non-zero when a session differs, after every run: then apply the totals rule to summary.json's statistics. Then the plugin row.
paired_rule_note: pass_rule is retained for gate parser validation; the registered verdict uses totals with accept=no-regress and the reachability and exact-session guards above.

plugin_canary.source: CANary hardware/canary-pwr-rev1.0, the original KiCad project at canary 2a7e070b, the current board base (git archive, unedited); never edit the source project.
plugin_canary.route: For each registered arm, run the release CLI on the plugin-exported DSN with the generated <stem>.args.json args verbatim, then append the arm's --router.profile, its explicit --router.java_quirks.shove_via_into_pending_piece flag, --stats json --stats-out <arm>/stats.json and --result-json=<arm>/result.json (no P04 bounds: the plugin's own options). One exported input and one argument list serve every arm. Compare each session with its own baseline arm's.
plugin_canary.grade: Grade each distinct session's imported copy with canary hardware/tools/grade.sh (GRADE_REV=2a7e070b; ses_import.py, kicad-cli pcb drc --schematic-parity --refill-zones --severity-all, via_in_pad.py, inner_tracks.py); arms with a byte-identical session share one grade. Record shorting_items and clearance separately. Retain export/import logs, versions, source hashes and grades.

not_registered: time (the fix changes no work budget beyond its own queries); the optimizer and passes past 3 on the DSN rows (P04's bounds); a KiCad grade of the DSN rows (GP8B and the others have no KiCad project here; the router's DRC guards them)

amendments.after: the registration was written and the implementer's one GP8B route per arm (no registered run yet)
amendments.change: `pairs` rewritten from {"verdict": [P1, P2], "reported": []} to the array [P1, P2], the form main 4d44676's parser reads for two judged pairs (`freerouting-dev gate --prereg --all-pairs` judges both, exit 1 if either fails); the same two verdict pairs, arms, boards, metrics and rule.
